references.authors: Aamir AB, Latif R, Sorath F, et al.
references.title: Acute kidney injury induced by topical hair straightening products: A systematic review.
references.finding: Systematic review of acute kidney injury after hair straightening (formaldehyde, glycolic and glyoxylic acid products): median onset 2 days, 6 needed dialysis, all recovered.

references.authors: Aiello AE, Larson EL, Levy SB
references.title: Consumer antibacterial soaps: effective or just risky?
references.finding: Systematic review: consumer soaps with 0.1-0.45% triclosan were no more effective than plain soap at preventing infectious symptoms or reducing hand bacteria; lab data showed cross-resistance to antibiotics.

references.authors: Allmyr M, Panagiotidis G, Sparve E, et al.
references.title: Human exposure to triclosan via toothpaste does not change CYP3A4 activity or plasma concentrations of thyroid hormones.
references.finding: Triclosan toothpaste raised plasma triclosan from 0.009-0.81 to 26-296 ng/g without changing CYP3A4 activity or thyroid hormones.

references.authors: Bertrand KA, Delp L, Coogan PF, et al.
references.title: Hair relaxer use and risk of uterine cancer in the Black Women's Health Study.
references.finding: Heavy hair-relaxer use was not associated with uterine cancer overall (HR 1.18, CI 0.81-1.71), but in postmenopausal women heavy and 20+ year use went with HRs of 1.64-1.71.

references.authors: Chang CJ, O'Brien KM, Keil AP, et al.
references.title: Use of Straighteners and Other Hair Products and Incident Uterine Cancer.
references.finding: Straightener use in the prior 12 months was associated with higher uterine cancer incidence (HR 1.80), 2.55 with more than 4 uses a year; dyes and perms were not associated.

references.authors: Dewalque L, Pirard C, Vandepaer S, et al.
references.title: Temporal variability of urinary concentrations of phthalate metabolites, parabens and benzophenone-3 in a Belgian adult population.
references.n: 32 adults, 11 spot urines each over 4 months
references.finding: A single spot urine reasonably represented 4-month exposure for parabens, benzophenone-3 and monoethyl phthalate, but not for DEHP metabolites.

references.authors: Estill CF, Mayer A, Slone J, et al.
references.title: Assessment of triphenyl phosphate (TPhP) exposure to nail salon workers by air, hand wipe, and urine analysis.
references.finding: Post-shift urinary DPHP (1.35 vs 0.84 ug/g creatinine pre-shift) and hand-wipe TPHP rose over the workday and correlated, pointing to dermal uptake in technicians.

references.authors: Gonzalez H, Farbrot A, Larkö O, et al.
references.title: Percutaneous absorption of the sunscreen benzophenone-3 after repeated whole-body applications, with and without ultraviolet irradiation.
references.finding: Volunteers excreted 1.2-8.7% of applied BP-3 in urine and were still excreting it 5 days after the last application; UV exposure did not change absorption.

references.authors: Gougeon A
references.title: Dynamics of follicular growth in the human: a model from preliminary results.
references.finding: The ovulatory follicle derives from a cohort of pre-antral follicles that began differentiating about 85 days earlier; final recruitment occurs 15-20 days before ovulation.

references.authors: Harley KG, Kogut K, Madrigal DS, et al.
references.title: Reducing Phthalate, Paraben, and Phenol Exposure from Personal Care Products in Adolescent Girls: Findings from the HERMOSA Intervention Study.
references.finding: Three days of products labelled free of phthalates, parabens, triclosan and BP-3 lowered urinary MEP 27%, methylparaben 44%, propylparaben 45%, triclosan 36% and BP-3 36%; ethyl- and butylparaben unexpectedly rose.

references.authors: HELLER CG, CLERMONT Y
references.title: Spermatogenesis in man: an estimate of its duration.
references.finding: One seminiferous epithelial cycle lasts about 16 days and spermatogenesis about 64 days.

references.authors: Huang K, Zhang X, Wang B, et al.
references.title: Accurate assessment of parabens exposure in healthy Chinese female adults: Findings from a multi-pathway exposure assessment coupled with intervention study.
references.finding: Personal-care products supplied over 99% of paraben exposure; unadjusted spot-urine intraclass correlations were poor (0.13-0.30) and improved only after kinetic modelling.

references.authors: Hutter HP, Wallner P, Hartl W, et al.
references.title: Higher blood concentrations of synthetic musks in women above fifty years than in younger women.
references.finding: Older women had higher plasma synthetic musks than younger women; galaxolide tracked frequent use of perfume, deodorant and shampoo.

references.authors: Janjua NR, Kongshoj B, Andersson AM, et al.
references.title: Sunscreens in human plasma and urine after repeated whole-body topical application.
references.finding: BP-3, 4-MBC and OMC appeared in plasma 1-2 h after first application; some 96-h plasma levels exceeded 24-h levels, suggesting accumulation.

references.authors: Jovanovic N, Bright F, Thomsen C, et al.
references.title: Levers to decrease exposure to harmful chemicals: the case of Personal Care Products and cosmetics.
references.finding: Refraining from usual personal-care products for 5 days lowered urinary phenoxyacetic acid 64%, BPA 39%, methylparaben 30% and MEP 22%, but several chemicals remained detectable; authors argue regulation would be more efficient and fairer.

references.authors: Kang H, Kim S, Lee H, et al.
references.title: Parabens, bisphenols, and other environmental phenols exposure from cosmetics use in Korean adolescent girls: Findings from a 2-day intervention study.
references.finding: A 2-day cosmetics restriction did not lower chemical levels overall; excluding non-users at baseline, BPA fell 33% and benzophenones 12-23%.

references.authors: Kim JH, Kwak JM, Kang H
references.title: Web-based behavioral intervention to reduce exposure to phthalate metabolites, bisphenol A, triclosan, and parabens in mothers with young children: A randomized controlled trial.
references.finding: A web-based behavioural intervention lowered urinary MEHP, MEOHP, BPA, methylparaben and propylparaben versus written information (decreases of 4-28% after one month).

references.authors: Li Y, Fletcher T, Mucs D, et al.
references.title: Half-lives of PFOS, PFHxS and PFOA after end of exposure to contaminated drinking water.
references.finding: After contaminated water was replaced, serum PFAS half-lives were 5.3 years for PFHxS, 3.4 for PFOS and 2.7 for PFOA.

references.authors: Matta MK, Zusterzeel R, Pilli NR, et al.
references.title: Effect of Sunscreen Application Under Maximal Use Conditions on Plasma Concentration of Sunscreen Active Ingredients: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
references.finding: Under maximal use (4 applications/day for 4 days), avobenzone, oxybenzone, octocrylene and ecamsule exceeded FDA's 0.5 ng/mL threshold on day 1; oxybenzone reached 169-210 ng/mL.

references.authors: Matta MK, Florian J, Zusterzeel R, et al.
references.title: Effect of Sunscreen Application on Plasma Concentration of Sunscreen Active Ingredients: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
references.finding: All six tested filters exceeded 0.5 ng/mL after a single application; oxybenzone peaked at 258 ng/mL (lotion) and homosalate at up to 23 ng/mL; authors say people should not stop using sunscreen.

references.authors: Meeker JD, Yang T, Ye X, et al.
references.title: Urinary concentrations of parabens and serum hormone levels, semen quality parameters, and sperm DNA damage.
references.finding: Methyl- and propylparaben were not associated with hormones, semen quality or sperm DNA damage; butylparaben categories tracked higher sperm DNA damage (p-trend 0.03).

references.authors: Mendelsohn E, Hagopian A, Hoffman K, et al.
references.title: Nail polish as a source of exposure to triphenyl phosphate.
references.finding: Painting nails with a polish containing 0.97% triphenyl phosphate raised its urinary metabolite DPHP about 7-fold 10-14 h later; gloves blocked most uptake, showing the route is dermal.

references.authors: Mohammed YH, Holmes A, Haridass IN, et al.
references.title: Support for the Safe Use of Zinc Oxide Nanoparticle Sunscreens: Lack of Skin Penetration or Cellular Toxicity after Repeated Application in Volunteers.
references.n: human volunteers, 5 days of repeated application
references.finding: Zinc oxide nanoparticle sunscreen stayed on the skin surface and in furrows and did not penetrate or harm the viable epidermis.

references.authors: Moos RK, Angerer J, Dierkes G, et al.
references.title: Metabolism and elimination of methyl, iso- and n-butyl paraben in human urine after single oral dosage.
references.finding: After oral dosing, 80-85% of the captured paraben metabolites were excreted in urine within 24 h; parent methylparaben made up 17% of the dose, butylparabens 6-7%.

references.authors: Nassan FL, Coull BA, Gaskins AJ, et al.
references.title: Personal Care Product Use in Men and Urinary Concentrations of Select Phthalate Metabolites and Parabens: Results from the Environment And Reproductive Health (EARTH) Study.
references.finding: Cologne/perfume and deodorant use raised urinary monoethyl phthalate by 83% and 74%; sunscreen and hand/body lotion raised urinary parabens by 66-156% and 79-147%, with the largest effects for use within 6 h of urine collection.

references.authors: Pierce JS, Abelmann A, Spicer LJ, et al.
references.title: Characterization of formaldehyde exposure resulting from the use of four professional hair straightening products.
references.finding: Keratin smoothing treatments produced airborne formaldehyde up to 1.19 ppm during application; even a product labelled formaldehyde-free released formaldehyde-releasing chemicals; estimated exposures can meet or exceed occupational limits.

references.authors: Rehfeld A, Dissing S, Skakkebæk NE
references.title: Chemical UV Filters Mimic the Effect of Progesterone on Ca(2+) Signaling in Human Sperm Cells.
references.finding: 13 of 29 UV filters induced calcium signals in human sperm in vitro, nine by activating the CatSper channel like progesterone, some at nanomolar levels and additively in mixtures.

references.authors: Samarasinghe SVAC, Krishnan K, Naidu R, et al.
references.title: Parabens generate reactive oxygen species in human spermatozoa.
references.finding: In vitro, parabens raised mitochondrial and cytosolic ROS in human sperm and reduced motility and viability in a chain-length-dependent way; methylparaben at clinically used concentrations raised ROS and oxidative DNA adducts but not DNA fragmentation.

references.authors: Sandborgh-Englund G, Adolfsson-Erici M, Odham G, et al.
references.title: Pharmacokinetics of triclosan following oral ingestion in humans.
references.finding: After 4 mg oral triclosan, plasma levels peaked within 1-3 h, the terminal plasma half-life was 21 h, and most was excreted within 24 h.

references.authors: Shen X, Zhan M, Wang Y, et al.
references.title: Exposure to parabens and semen quality in reproductive-aged men.
references.finding: A paraben mixture was associated with lower sperm concentration, total count and progressive motility; butylparaben and methylparaben were the main contributors.

references.authors: Shin MY, Choi JW, Lee S, et al.
references.title: Pharmacokinetics of transdermal methyl-, ethyl-, and propylparaben in humans following single dermal administration.
references.finding: After a single whole-arm dermal application of labelled methyl-, ethyl- and propylparaben, terminal half-lives were 9.3-12.2 h, longer than after oral intake, with a larger share of unconjugated (active) paraben in blood.

references.authors: Singh J, Mumford SL, Pollack AZ, et al.
references.title: Tampon use, environmental chemicals and oxidative stress in the BioCycle study.
references.finding: Tampon users had non-significantly higher blood mercury (25%) and urinary isoprostane (about 5%) than non-users; no association with inflammation markers.

references.authors: Smith KW, Braun JM, Williams PL, et al.
references.title: Predictors and variability of urinary paraben concentrations in men and women, including before and during pregnancy.
references.n: fertility-clinic men and women with repeated urine samples
references.finding: Intraclass correlations for methyl- and propylparaben were 0.42-0.54, so a single urine sample reasonably ranked exposure over several months; concentrations were 3.8 times higher in African American participants.

references.authors: Wise LA, Palmer JR, Reich D, et al.
references.title: Hair relaxer use and risk of uterine leiomyomata in African-American women.
references.finding: Ever use of hair relaxers was associated with 17% higher incidence of uterine fibroids, with trends for frequency, duration and number of scalp burns.

references.authors: Wise LA, Wang TR, Ncube CN, et al.
references.title: Use of Chemical Hair Straighteners and Fecundability in a North American Preconception Cohort.
references.finding: Hair relaxer use was associated with slightly lower fecundability (current FR 0.81, CI 0.64-1.03; former 0.89, CI 0.81-0.98; 10+ years 0.71), with non-monotonic patterns.

timing.summary: Parabens are short-lived: urine levels track product use within hours and fall within a few days of switching. Levels stay fairly stable over months only because people keep the same product habits.

onset.text: Use of lotion or sunscreen within 6 h of urine collection strongly raised urinary parabens [epc-nassan2017]; dermal absorption peaks over several hours [epc-shin2023].

full.text: With daily use levels reach a steady state within a day or two, given a dermal half-life of about 9-12 h [epc-shin2023] (extrapolated).

after_stopping.text: 80-85% of an oral dose is excreted within 24 h [epc-moos2016]; switching to paraben-free products cut methylparaben 30-45% within 3-5 days [epc-harley2016, epc-jovanovic2026].

frequency.text: Every application adds a new pulse, so exposure depends on how often leave-on products are used; habits are stable enough that one urine sample ranks exposure moderately well over months [epc-smith2012].

timing.debate: Whether one spot urine captures long-term exposure is disputed: moderate reliability in clinic cohorts [epc-smith2012, epc-dewalque2015] versus poor reliability in a small controlled-use study [epc-huang2021].

sperm.late_start: Switching 2-4 weeks before still removes parabens from semen and from any sample collected with a lubricant for IVF or IUI, which is where direct-contact effects are shown.
sperm.text: Spermatogenesis takes about 64 days plus epididymal transit [epc-heller1963], so a chemical that affected developing sperm would need roughly 2-3 months off exposure before a full cohort of unexposed sperm is ejaculated.

egg.late_start: Switching 2-4 weeks before still lowers exposure during the final, rapid growth of the dominant follicle and in early pregnancy.
egg.text: The ovulated follicle began its final growth phase about 85 days earlier and is recruited 15-20 days before ovulation [epc-gougeon1986], so a follicle-level effect would need about 3 months off exposure to clear.

timing.summary: Triclosan has a plasma half-life of about a day, so personal levels fall within days of switching products. Population levels fell after the 2016-2017 FDA rule removed it from consumer washes.

onset.text: Plasma triclosan peaked 1-3 h after an oral dose [epc-sandborgh2006]; toothpaste use raised plasma levels markedly within 14 days [epc-allmyr2009].

full.text: Steady state with daily use within a few days, given a 21-h half-life [epc-sandborgh2006] (extrapolated).

after_stopping.text: Most of a dose is excreted within 24 h and 24-83% within 4 days [epc-sandborgh2006]; labelled-free products cut urinary triclosan 36% in 3 days [epc-harley2016].

frequency.text: Exposure tracks daily product use; there is no benefit of antibacterial soap over plain soap at any frequency [epc-aiello2007].

timing.debate: No substantive published debate on timing found.

sperm.late_start: Stopping late still lowers exposure of sperm in the final maturation stages; benefit is unproven either way.
sperm.text: Spermatogenesis takes about 64 days plus epididymal transit [epc-heller1963], so a chemical that affected developing sperm would need roughly 2-3 months off exposure before a full cohort of unexposed sperm is ejaculated.

egg.late_start: Stopping late still lowers exposure during final follicle growth and early pregnancy.
egg.text: The ovulated follicle began its final growth phase about 85 days earlier and is recruited 15-20 days before ovulation [epc-gougeon1986], so a follicle-level effect would need about 3 months off exposure to clear.

timing.summary: Organic UV filters reach the blood within hours of the first application and build up with repeated daily use; oxybenzone is still excreted days after the last application. Exposure is seasonal and tied to how much skin is covered.

onset.text: BP-3, 4-MBC and OMC appeared in plasma 1-2 h after the first application [epc-janjua2008]; all six FDA-tested filters exceeded 0.5 ng/mL on day 1 [epc-matta2020].

full.text: Plasma levels kept rising over 4 days of repeated application, with some 96-h levels above 24-h levels [epc-janjua2008, epc-matta2019].

after_stopping.text: BP-3 was still being excreted in urine 5 days after the last of 5 days of use [epc-gonzalez2006]; full washout time is not well defined.

frequency.text: Daily sunscreen is beneficial for skin (see the sunscreen factor); filter exposure scales with applications and body area, so mineral products and clothing reduce it without giving up protection [epc-mohammed2019].

timing.debate: Whether persistence after stopping reflects tissue accumulation is unsettled: 96-h levels exceeded 24-h levels in one study [epc-janjua2008], and BP-3 excretion continued for 5 days in another [epc-gonzalez2006].

sperm.late_start: Switching to mineral sunscreen a few weeks before still lowers filter levels in semen around conception, relevant to the in-vitro CatSper effect.
sperm.text: Spermatogenesis takes about 64 days plus epididymal transit [epc-heller1963], so a chemical that affected developing sperm would need roughly 2-3 months off exposure before a full cohort of unexposed sperm is ejaculated.

timing.summary: The phthalate part of fragrance (diethyl phthalate) clears within days, but lipophilic synthetic musks accumulate in blood and fat, and levels were higher in older women. Musk half-lives in people have not been measured well.

onset.text: Urinary MEP rose sharply with cologne or perfume use within 6 h of collection [epc-nassan2017].

full.text: Musks keep accumulating with long-term use; older women had higher plasma musks than younger women [epc-hutter2010]. Time course not measured.

after_stopping.text: MEP fell 22-27% within 3-5 days of switching products [epc-harley2016, epc-jovanovic2026]; musk washout not measured.

frequency.text: Less frequent and less skin-area use of fragranced leave-on products lowers both MEP and musk exposure; no schedule has been tested.

timing.debate: No substantive published debate on timing found.

timing.summary: Acute harms (formaldehyde irritation, glyoxylic-acid kidney injury) appear within days of a treatment, while cancer and fertility associations reflect years of use. How long risk persists after stopping is not known; former relaxer users still had slightly lower fecundability.

onset.text: Acute kidney injury after glyoxylic-acid straightening appeared at a median of 2 days [epc-aamir2025]; airborne formaldehyde peaks during the treatment itself [epc-pierce2011].

full.text: Cancer associations relate to frequent use over years (20+ years in postmenopausal women [epc-bertrand2023]); not a defined plateau.

after_stopping.text: Not measured; former relaxer users had fecundability ratio 0.89 versus never users [epc-wise2023], so any effect may outlast use.

frequency.text: Uterine cancer risk was highest with more than 4 straightener uses a year [epc-chang2022]; fewer treatments and no scalp burns are the practical levers [epc-wise2012].

egg.late_start: Stopping late avoids acute formaldehyde and chemical exposure in early pregnancy, but whether it restores fecundability is unknown.
egg.text: No study measured how fecundability changes after stopping; former users still showed slightly lower fecundability [epc-wise2023]. The 100 days follows the follicle growth period [epc-gougeon1986] (extrapolated).

timing.debate: No substantive published debate on timing found.

timing.summary: Polish chemicals are absorbed through the skin around the nails and peak in urine within half a day. Workplace solvent exposure repeats every shift; UV-lamp DNA damage in cells is permanent once mutations form.

onset.text: Urinary DPHP rose about 7-fold 10-14 h after nail painting [epc-mendelsohn2016]; technicians' urinary DPHP rose across a work shift [epc-estill2021].

full.text: Peak at 10-14 h after a single application [epc-mendelsohn2016].

after_stopping.text: Return to baseline not precisely measured; urine was followed for about 24 h in the glove substudy [epc-mendelsohn2016].

frequency.text: Each manicure is a short pulse; frequent painting or gel sessions and daily salon work multiply exposure. No schedule studies exist.

timing.debate: No substantive published debate on timing found.

timing.summary: No study has measured how body levels of metals or other chemicals change with tampon use or after switching products. Timing is unknown.

after_stopping.text: Not measured; the only biomarker study compared users and non-users cross-sectionally [epc-singh2019].

frequency.text: Change tampons as directed and use the lowest absorbency needed; no evidence on chemical exposure by frequency.

timing.debate: No substantive published debate on timing found.

timing.summary: Long-chain PFAS stay in the blood for years, so removing a cosmetic or floss source lowers body levels only slowly. Short-chain PFAS clear faster but their dermal contribution is modelled, not measured.

onset.text: Not measured for cosmetics or floss.

full.text: Not measured; with half-lives of years, levels approach steady state over many years of use (extrapolated from [epc-li2018]).

after_stopping.text: Serum half-lives after a source is removed were 2.7 years (PFOA), 3.4 (PFOS) and 5.3 (PFHxS) [epc-li2018].

frequency.text: Because PFAS accumulate, cumulative use matters more than frequency; non-PTFE floss removes the floss source entirely.

timing.debate: No substantive published debate on timing found.

timing.summary: Switching to products free of specific short-lived chemicals lowers their urine levels within 2-5 days, and the reduction lasts as long as the habit does. It does not change persistent chemicals.

onset.text: Reductions of 22-45% in MEP, parabens, triclosan and BP-3 after 3-5 days [epc-harley2016, epc-jovanovic2026]; no reduction in 2 days among low users [epc-kang2025].

full.text: A web-based programme sustained reductions over 1 month [epc-kim2021].

after_stopping.text: Not measured directly; given half-lives of hours to a day, levels return within days of resuming old products (extrapolated from [epc-shin2023, epc-sandborgh2006]).

frequency.text: The benefit lasts only while the low-exposure products are used every day.

timing.debate: Whether short switches work for everyone is contested: large drops in Latina teenagers and French young women [epc-harley2016, epc-jovanovic2026] versus no overall change in Korean girls who used few products [epc-kang2025].
